observation: The core is a Delphi application first shipped in 1998 with a web layer bolted on in 2013; the settlement engine has zero automated test coverage and runs on an unsupported database version. Technical risk is generational, not incremental.
why_accepted: Reviewer kept the model's two verified facts and added the generational framing the model missed; every claim traces to p10.

observation: Growth of 2% leaves little room to out-run problems organically. With EBITDA positive the hold thesis can work - but only if retention is genuinely strong, and the one metric that would show it is the one the document does not provide. Treat retention as the deciding diligence item.
why_accepted: Original applied a venture-exit lens to a permanent-capital profile and restated computed figures. Reviewer rewrote it to connect growth thinness to the missing retention data - the actual decision-relevant chain.

observation: There is no CTO and no documented succession plan behind the one person who writes production code for the settlement logic.
why_accepted: Same facts as the draft, tightened: the original's 'succession plan for its only employee' garbled who the plan was missing for.
